about: The host's frame diagnostics (frame-diagnostics.h; sample/FrameProbe.tsx; docs/performance.mdx, "Reading the session's log"), each of the host's two threads its own (docs/adr/0067-the-ui-thread.mdx): a frame of the UI thread's whose work takes longer than a refresh of its display writes one line to the session's log naming what started it and where its time went, and so does a stretch of JavaScript's work on its thread longer than a refresh, at most one a second each, with how many went unsaid. Presses answered at once write none; a press whose JavaScript holds its thread 120 ms writes one line of JavaScript's (at least 100 ms, the window free to present meanwhile) and no slow frame, the frame showing its answer timed from the press (at least 100 ms); 90 frames of requestAnimationFrame stay within a refresh (every run checks a frame is said to be slow exactly when its work passes a refresh, and each frame counts JavaScript's work since the frame before); and while the window draws, a summary every 10 s whose numbers are those of the frames and of JavaScript's stretches in its report (regress.py checks every summary of every run), and none while it is idle.

steps.name: a press answered at once: no slow frame
a press whose JavaScript holds its thread 120 ms: one line of JavaScript's, no slow frame, the answer's frame timed from the press
three such presses within a second: three slow stretches of JavaScript, one line
the next line of JavaScript's says the two not shown
90 frames of requestAnimationFrame, each drawn: nearly all within a refresh
idle: the frames since the last summary summed up once, within 10 s of the first, then nothing

logged: ^\[host so\.oxy\.frameprobe\] in the last 1\d\.\d s: \d+ frames, their work [\d.]+ ms median
